source_text: Si lepra totum corpus operuerit et alba fuerit, mundus est. Totalis confessio candidum facit. Qui partem tegit, manet immundus.
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical rule about leprosy to confession of sin: a leprosy that covers the whole body and turns white is clean, and so total confession makes a person clean.
pass_a_gloss: If leprosy covers the whole body and is white, he is clean. Total confession makes white. He who covers a part remains unclean.

choices.why: Keeps the ritual sense of clean as the opposite of unclean, matching the glossary's immundus as unclean.
Renders totalis literally to preserve the parallel with the whole body covered by leprosy.
Keeps the physical whiteness image that links the leprosy's whiteness to the cleansing effect of confession.
Uses the glossary term unclean for immundus and keeps the durative force of manet.

bible_refs.note: Si lepra totum corpus operuerit et alba fuerit, mundus est

pass_b_english: If leprosy covers the whole body and is white, the person is clean (Leviticus 13:13). Total confession makes a person white. The one who covers only part remains unclean.

last_rejected.quote: Total confession makes a person white. The one who covers only part remains unclean.
last_rejected.source_quote: Totalis confessio candidum facit. Qui partem tegit, manet immundus.
last_rejected.why: English hides that these are Origen's interpretive comments, not Scripture text.
last_rejected.fix: Total confession makes one white. Whoever covers only part remains unclean.
last_rejected.ruling: Source has no speaker markers; English faithfully renders both sentences. Formatting is editorial, not a translation error.
